title: GRP75-dependent SIMPA mediates inter-organellar quality control
title_zh: GRP75依赖性SIMPA介导的跨细胞器质量控制
abstract: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress1. Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health2–7. However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light–electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness. Proteotoxic stress drives formation of GRP75-dependent protein aggregates that signal through mitochondria–ER contact sites to activate targeted quality-control pathways, enabling selective clearance of damaged proteins and preserving mitochondrial integrity.
abstract_zh: 线粒体由双层膜包裹，是半自主细胞器，因此对全局和内部蛋白稳态应激极为敏感1。为维持线粒体完整性和细胞健康，进化出了多种蛋白稳态和跨细胞器水平的监控机制2–7。然而，蛋白稳态损伤如何跨细胞器传递应激信号以及质量监控机械如何协调这些功能的精确机制仍不清楚。我们在此报道，在蛋白稳态应激下，受损的线粒体蛋白被隔离形成应激诱导的线粒体蛋白聚集体（SIMPA），以空间受限的方式激活特定的质量控制机制而不扰动线粒体网络。定量蛋白组学和相关光-电镜分析揭示，SIMPA通过线粒体-内质网接触位点或线粒体相关膜介导跨细胞器通讯。从机制上看，GRP75协调SIMPA的生成，并通过线粒体-内质网接触位点或线粒体相关膜局部激活内质网未折叠蛋白反应通路，以靶向清除SIMPAs。在功能上，在细胞和肝脏疾病模型中，我们发现GRP75依赖的SIMPA信号级联减轻线粒体应激，并在蛋白毒性应激下维持线粒体完整性。总体而言，我们表明，SIMPAs作为蛋白质凝聚体，作为线粒体质量控制的中心跨隔室通讯枢纽发挥作用，支持细胞和有机体的适应性。蛋白毒性应激驱动GRP75依赖性蛋白聚集体的形成，通过线粒体-内质网接触位点进行信号传递以激活靶向质量控制通路，从而实现受损蛋白的选择性清除并维持线粒体完整性。
